stimulus.text: The village of Kherwadi repaired its old well in April after a survey found that the water level had dropped by two metres in five years. A committee of eight residents was formed, and each household agreed to contribute ₹150 a year for upkeep. In the first season after the repair, the committee recorded that the well supplied water for 210 days without running dry, compared with 150 days in the previous year. The committee’s secretary pointed out that the monsoon was heavier than usual this year, so the longer supply could not be credited to the repair alone. The committee has therefore proposed to keep measuring the water level every month for three more years before deciding whether to dig a second well.
